title: Stage 2: Tidy the scanner inbox
summary: Rename-ScanByDate: a bulk rename with a dry run, that can be run twice without doing damage.

steps.title: The scanner inbox
body: The office scanner drops `scan0001.pdf`, `scan0002.pdf`, ... into a share (`~/scans`). Nobody can find anything.
The ask: rename each to **`yyyy-MM-dd_HHmm_<original name>`** by when it was scanned (its `LastWriteTime`), so
the folder sorts by date and the original name is kept for reference.
A bulk rename that runs every hour must be:
- **rehearsable**: `-WhatIf` shows the plan and changes nothing;
- **idempotent**: running it twice is the same as once (already renamed files are left alone);
- **careful**: it never overwrites an existing file; it skips and warns instead.
`-f` formats dates with .NET format strings: `'{0:yyyy-MM-dd_HHmm}' -f $file.LastWriteTime` gives
`2026-11-14_1402`. (Lowercase `mm` is minutes, uppercase `MM` months: the classic mix-up.)

steps.explain: `mm` is minutes (05), not the month. File names with dates should always be `yyyy-MM-dd`: they sort correctly as text.

steps.title: Rename-ScanByDate
prompt: - `-Path` (mandatory, an existing folder); only the `.pdf` files directly in it;
- renames each to `yyyy-MM-dd_HHmm_<name>` from its `LastWriteTime`, and **outputs the renamed files**;
- **skips** files that already start with such a date (so a second run changes nothing);
- never overwrites: if the target name exists, warn and skip;
Try it with `-WhatIf` on `~/scans` first. The checks run it on fresh copies of the inbox.

checks.name: dry run, rename, and a second run that changes nothing
checks.fail: Not quite (see what the check found).

hints: `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Path -File -Filter *.pdf | Where-Object Name -notmatch '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}_\d{4}_'` skips the ones already done.
solution: Renames scanner PDFs to yyyy-MM-dd_HHmm_<name>.pdf by when they were scanned.
explain: `return` inside `ForEach-Object` ends the script block for **that** item only (like `continue` in a loop). Note
what the function trusts: `LastWriteTime`. Copying files with some tools resets it; for photos, the date in the
EXIF data is more reliable, which is why real photo tools read it instead.
